Hi Neha / Marissa,

We're preparing to submit a formal data deletion request under GDPR for a subset of our end users and procurement has asked a couple of practical questions about what that will mean for our billing records:

- If Ledgerium requests deletion of our end-user data, will Redwood also delete invoices and the usage ledger entries tied to those users?
- What retention periods do you apply to invoice PDFs and to token-level usage logs used for billing disputes?
- Can personal identifiers on invoices (billing contact, email) be redacted while retaining the invoice/ledger for tax/audit purposes?
- Is it possible to keep accounting copies in an EU-only storage region to satisfy our auditors?

Procurement needs a short written statement they can attach to the deletion request. Can you confirm what Redwood can and cannot delete, and what options we have for residency or redaction?

Thanks — would appreciate a reply by EOD PST if possible so we can keep the procurement timeline.

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear questions. Quick summary up front, then details and next steps.

Short answer: We can honor erasure of personal data where required, but invoices and accounting-ledger entries required by law or tax regulation must be retained. Where feasible, we can redact personal identifiers from retained records and offer EU-only storage for enterprise accounts under an addendum.

Details:
- Invoice PDFs and core accounting ledger: retained for statutory and audit requirements. Typical retention window we maintain on Hosted accounts is 7 years (to satisfy common tax/audit retention in major jurisdictions). These records are considered accounting documents and are excluded from consumer erasure where law requires retention.

- Token-level usage logs (raw per-request logs): retained for billing accuracy and dispute resolution. Standard retention for these logs is 13 months for Hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private deployments this can be negotiated in the contract. We can provide summarized/aggregated usage exports sooner on request.

- Redaction: Where an invoice or ledger entry contains personal identifiers (billing contact name/email), we can redact those fields in the retained copy to the extent it doesn't invalidate the legal/accounting integrity of the document. For example, we can replace email addresses and user names with hashed IDs and keep invoice numbers, amounts, and dates intact. Full redaction of amounts/dates would typically not be permitted because that would defeat the record's purpose.

- Data residency: For Hosted customers invoices and billing records are normally stored in our standard regions (which may include US-based storage). For EU-only residency of billing artifacts we offer options on Dedicated or Private plans, or via an addendum where we store accounting artifacts and backups in EU-only storage. We can also export a certified copy of invoices to your preferred EU storage (S3 bucket or secure Share) if you require custody.

Next steps I recommend:
1) I can produce a short procurement-friendly statement that you can attach to the deletion request (one-paragraph plus bullets).
2) If you need EU-only residency for invoices, let me know whether you have a Dedicated/Private contract or want to discuss an addendum; I'll loop in our sales/solutions engineer.
3) For specific invoice numbers or user IDs you plan to erase, send those to me and we'll map which records are considered accounting-retained vs erasable.

I'm attaching a one-page retention summary for your review. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call with procurement if that helps.

Cheers,

Hi Laura — attached is a short procurement statement (PDF). Quick answers to your follow-ups below and a couple of options.

- Billing emails / PDF attachments: if a deletion request targets PERSONAL DATA contained in billing emails (e.g., a billing contact's personal email, name), we can redact those fields from retained artifacts; however the invoice objects themselves (invoice number, amounts, dates) will be retained for accounting.

- Residency options: 1) If you already have a Dedicated/Private arrangement we can enable EU-only storage for billing artifacts. 2) If you're on Hosted, we can provide an export of historical invoices to an EU S3 bucket you control and add an amendment to store future invoices in EU-only storage for new billing cycles (requires procurement approval).

Please see the attached PDF for the procurement statement and a brief summary of residency options. If procurement signs off, we can execute a custodian export and a redaction plan for the specified user IDs.

Best,
Neha
